title: SLO specification (S4 slo lens's second artifact)
description: docs/decisions/011 Finding 1: an SLO specification is not expressible as a list of event attributes the way design_fragment's signals are -- an indicator, objective, paired-window burn-rate alert tiers, and an error-budget policy are a different shape. Emitted alongside design_fragment by the slo lens (lenses[].emits, docs/decisions/020). budget_fraction and detection_window are declared inputs; burn_rate_multiplier is computed from them and gate-verified (oah/design/slo_gates.py); short_window_rationale is required prose because the pack can compute the first and cannot derive the second (docs/decisions/011 Finding 3 -- the one-twelfth short-window ratio some published SLO guides use has no derivation in any reviewed source, so this schema requires a stated rationale per tier rather than silently assuming that ratio).

surface_point_ids.description: Which surface_map.json points this SLO covers -- typically the http_server_route/declarative_route points for one critical business journey.

good_event_definition.description: The concrete predicate distinguishing a good event from a bad one, e.g. 'http.server.request.duration sample with error.type absent' (docs/decisions/012 finding 6: error.type is stable + conditionally required on the HTTP duration histograms, so this is computable from metrics alone).

aggregation_method.description: How the indicator's value is computed from raw events. 'ratio_of_counts' (good/total) and 'raw_histogram_bucket' (a real percentile computed once, over the true underlying distribution) are valid. 'single_pass_percentile' names the same thing as 'raw_histogram_bucket' when the source is a single histogram, not an average -- there is deliberately NO enum value for averaging multiple precomputed percentiles (e.g. averaging each instance's own local p99), which is not a valid percentile of the combined distribution and is a real, common statistical error this schema refuses to name as a legitimate option.

target.description: e.g. 0.999. Never 1.0 -- a target of exactly 1.0 declares zero error budget, which makes every alert tier's burn-rate math meaningless (any failure at all exhausts the budget instantly) and is never a real operational target.

period_days.description: e.g. 30 -- the window the target and error budget are computed over.

up_predicate.description: The concrete condition under which this indicator counts as 'up' for a given time slice.

granularity.description: The time-slice size the up_predicate is evaluated at, e.g. '1m', '5m'.

brownout_classification.description: How a partial-degradation state (elevated latency/error rate short of full outage) is classified against this objective -- an SLO with no answer here silently either double-counts or ignores brownouts, both wrong.

budget_fraction.description: Fraction of the total error budget this tier alerts on consuming, e.g. 0.02 for 2%.

short_window_hours.description: A second, shorter window paired with detection_window_hours (multi-window burn-rate alerting) so a real spike alerts fast without a single-window alert also firing on noise.

short_window_rationale.description: Required prose, not a formula -- docs/decisions/011 Finding 3 found no derivation anywhere in the reviewed corpus for the specific short-window ratio (e.g. detection_window / 12) some published guides use uncredited. State why THIS window was chosen, not just that a window exists.

burn_rate_multiplier.description: Computed, not asserted: budget_fraction * (period_days * 24) / detection_window_hours -- gate-verified against the other three fields (oah/design/slo_gates.py's check_burn_rate_matches_declared_inputs).

entry_criterion_tier.description: Must name a tier that actually exists in this spec's own alert_tiers[] -- gate-verified, never a dangling reference.

exit_criterion.description: The concrete, checkable condition under which this policy step ends -- required for every step, same discipline design_fragment.schema.json's decision_menu_steps already applies to pause/freeze/throttle.
